analysis.title: Core Convictions (Multi-Asset Rundown)
key_insights: UBS is positive on US equities into 2027. Its core call is to lean into derated growth: the S&P 500 P/E has fallen about 20% (driven by semis) while 2026 EPS is on track to grow about 30%.
Historically, after a P/E derating of more than 10%, the S&P 500 has returned a median 20% over the following year.

UBS says the three drivers of higher risk premia (AI disappointment fears, higher yields and spreads, weaker buybacks) now look close to turning. Cloud growth nearly tripled between Q3 and Q1, and net buybacks outside the hyperscalers should rise by $200-400bn next year.
Trade: long NDX vs RTY, citing near-2022 relative P/E lows for about 2x the forward EPS growth.

European equities: buy second-order AI capex plays (Materials, Semi equipment, Electrification) and second-wave fiscal winners (Infrastructure, Renewables). First-wave AI suppliers are sold out and support about EUR1.7tn of European stocks with light positioning and accelerating revisions.

US rates: hot inflation data raises the risk that the Fed delivers more than the two further hikes in UBS's baseline. After the recent flattening, 1y-forward 5s30s SOFR steepeners offer attractive risk/reward, and faster duration supply in 2027 adds steepening pressure.

Euro area: the inflation peak is still ahead, with energy the key upside risk. UBS likes 2s10s ESTR flatteners (at 17bp, target -20bp, stop 35bp) and expects wider spreads in France and Italy ahead of next year's elections.
FX: recent USD strength has brought key pairs toward year-end targets (EURUSD 1.1050, USDJPY 160, USDCHF 0.84). UBS sees scope for further USD strength into 2027, targeting EURUSD 1.07 by end-Q2.

GBP resilience is expected (EURGBP 0.8350 year-end, 0.82 from end-Q2). UBS is bearish SEK (EURSEK 11.20 end-2026, 11.50 end-2027) and structurally bullish NOK into 2027. It prefers fading NZD strength.

Credit: US IG/HY/LL spreads tightened w/w to 86/312/493bp after Coreweave earnings. UBS took profits on its CDX HY short and sees balanced year-end spread risks. Distress ratios are rising in HY and loans (7.4%/9.1%), driven by rate-sensitive Tech and Telecoms.
European IG looks appealing versus US IG because European spreads have priced more of the rates shock. France remains a key risk, but UBS sees French spreads nearing a balanced level.

EM: UBS expects 2027 returns of 15% for equities, 6% for local debt and 5% for credit, with FX and rate tailwinds in H2. Korea tech (13% of MSCI EM) risk/reward is compelling, as market-implied Samsung and Hynix EBITDA discounts imply an end to the AI cycle by 2028, which UBS sees as unlikely.
EM FX and rates: sell EUR vs CNH and BRL, long USD/PLN, short CLP vs COP and IDR vs THB. Long MXN 2y2y and HUF 10y vs Poland local debt.

Macro backdrop: the AI build-out accounts for over half of global trade growth, most of US investment growth and close to half of this year's equity gains, with little sign of capex broadening or a productivity pickup. Outside tech/AI, global activity is tracking slightly sub-trend.
UBS published its Global Economics & Markets Outlook 2027/2028, with 20 essays, 15 trade ideas and scenarios on oil prices, much higher bond yields and AI disappointment.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings growth of about 30% in 2026 against a roughly 20% P/E derating, with risk-premia drivers close to turning.
Second-order AI capex beneficiaries as first-wave AI suppliers are sold out and expanding capacity.
Second-wave fiscal winners as German infrastructure revisions turn positive and EU recovery-fund payments are largely spent in 2027.
Funded leg of the long NDX vs RTY trade: near-2022 relative valuations but about half the forward EPS growth.
Risk/reward is compelling because market-implied Samsung and Hynix EBITDA discounts price an end to the AI cycle by 2028.

earnings_insights: UBS says 2026 S&P 500 EPS is on track to grow about 30%.

UBS notes q/q cloud growth nearly tripled between Q3 and Q1, per its estimate.

risk_factors: Outlook is unusually dependent on a handful of tech firms, with little sign of capex broadening or a productivity pickup.
Hot inflation data could force the Fed beyond two further hikes.
A cold winter or another supply shock could revive euro area inflation concerns.
French political risk ahead of next year's elections.
Rising distress in HY and loans, driven by rate-sensitive Tech and Telecoms.
Near-term EM local debt outlook is challenging, with tailwinds only in H2 2027.
vol_and_positioning: European first-wave AI suppliers supporting about EUR1.7tn of stocks have light positioning and accelerating revisions.

geopolitical: Energy markets and supply chains remain disrupted, extending central bank tightening cycles.
Elections next year in France and Italy are expected to widen spreads in those markets.
Early elections are a near-term political risk in the UK.
NZ election results reduced the risk of a return to a dual-mandate RBNZ.

tension_points.bull_case: EPS is on track to grow about 30% in 2026 while the P/E fell about 20%. Historically a >10% derating is followed by a median 20% SPX return, and cloud growth and buybacks are turning.
tension_points.bear_case: AI disappointment fears, higher yields and spreads, and weaker buybacks raised risk premia. The outlook is unusually dependent on a handful of tech firms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The three risk-premia drivers (AI concerns, yields and spreads, buybacks) failing to turn.
